title: server/src/config/specialtyTemplates.js — complete recon for the .NET 10 port (specialty exam templates, template resolution, and SOAP-prompt formatters)

findings.name: SPECIALTY_TEMPLATES — top-level structure and insertion order
findings.behaviour: A plain object literal keyed by template key. 11 entries, in this EXACT insertion order (this order is observable — it drives `allTemplates` in the API response and the picker dropdown): ophthalmology, cardiology, neurology, orthopedics, pediatrics, pulmonology, internal_medicine, dermatology, obgyn, psychiatry, ent. Each value is `{ key, label, icon, sections }` in that property order; `key` always duplicates its own dictionary key. `sections` is an array of `{ title, paired?, fields }`; `fields` is an array of `{ key, label, type, unit?, options?, placeholder? }`. Totals: 34 sections, 117 fields, 117 DISTINCT field keys across all templates — zero collisions (verified). No template has an empty `sections` array and no section has an empty `fields` array, so `getFieldMapForPrompt` never returns '' for a valid key. Nothing here is loaded from DB, env, or disk: it is a frozen-in-source constant, and the module is `require`d lazily inside each route handler (lines 38, 63, 720) rather than at file top.
findings.portRecommendation: Owner: a new `Tebrazi.Api/Configuration/SpecialtyTemplates.cs` (or `Tebrazi.Domain.Visits.Config`). Recommend a `static class SpecialtyTemplates` exposing `static IReadOnlyDictionary<string, SpecialtyTemplate> All` built from an **embedded JSON resource** (`specialtyTemplates.json`) deserialized once in a static ctor, NOT hand-written object initializers — see the 'embedded JSON vs records' finding for why. Order must be preserved: back `All` with an insertion-ordered structure (build a `List<SpecialtyTemplate>` from the JSON array and a `Dictionary` index over it) because `System.Collections.Generic.Dictionary` order is an implementation detail you must not rely on for `allTemplates`.

findings.name: Complete field schema — representative template (obgyn) with exact JSON
findings.behaviour:
obgyn is the best representative because it is the only template that exercises all five field types AND the only one with a field that has neither `unit` nor `placeholder`. Literal JSON the client receives (from `GET /api/visits/specialty-template/obgyn`, body `{"template": <this>}`):
{"key":"obgyn","label":"OB/GYN Exam","icon":"🤰","sections":[{"title":"Obstetric History","fields":[{"key":"lmp","label":"LMP","type":"date"},{"key":"gravida","label":"Gravida","type":"number","placeholder":"1"},{"key":"para","label":"Para","type":"number","placeholder":"0"},{"key":"gestational_age","label":"Gestational Age","type":"text","placeholder":"32+4 weeks"}]},{"title":"Obstetric Examination","fields":[{"key":"fundal_height","label":"Fundal Height","type":"number","unit":"cm","placeholder":"32"},{"key":"fhr","label":"Fetal Heart Rate","type":"number","unit":"bpm","placeholder":"140"},{"key":"presentation","label":"Presentation","type":"select","options":["Cephalic","Breech","Transverse","Oblique","Not assessed"]},{"key":"cervical_exam","label":"Cervical Exam","type":"text","placeholder":"Dilation, effacement, station"}]},{"title":"Gynecologic Notes","fields":[{"key":"us_notes","label":"Ultrasound Notes","type":"textarea","placeholder":"Biometry, AFI, placenta, anomalies"},{"key":"gyn_exam","label":"Gynecologic Exam","type":"textarea","placeholder":"Speculum, bimanual, cervix, adnexa"}]}]}

Field-type vocabulary (exactly 5 lowercase strings): text, number, textarea, select, date. The client's FieldRenderer (client/src/components/SpecialtyExamCard.jsx:234) switches on `select` / `textarea` / `date` and falls through to `<input type={type==='number'?'number':'text'}>` for everything else, so an unknown type degrades to a text box rather than erroring.

Unit vocabulary (exactly 7 strings, on exactly 11 fields): "mmHg" (iop_od, iop_os), "%" (echo_ef, fev1_fvc), "/15" (gcs), "cm" (head_circumference, fundal_height), "% predicted" (fev1, fvc), "L/min" (peak_flow), "bpm" (fhr).

`paired: true` appears on exactly 6 sections (all 5 ophthalmology sections + ENT's "Ear") and is NEVER present as `false` — absence means unpaired. The client uses it only to force a 2-column grid (SpecialtyExamCard.jsx:210).
findings.portRecommendation: C# shape: `public sealed record SpecialtyTemplate(string Key, string Label, string Icon, IReadOnlyList<TemplateSection> Sections);` `public sealed record TemplateSection(string Title, bool? Paired, IReadOnlyList<TemplateField> Fields);` `public sealed record TemplateField(string Key, string Label, string Type, string? Unit, IReadOnlyList<string>? Options, string? Placeholder);` — declare the positional parameters in exactly that order (STJ serializes CLR property declaration order, and the client's JSON is byte-compared). Keep `Type`/`Unit` as plain `string`, not enums, so a future value round-trips verbatim.

Naming convention the client depends on: `_od`/`_r` suffix = right side (blue), `_os`/`_l` suffix = left side (green) — SpecialtyExamCard.jsx:256-258. Renaming any field key breaks the side colouring and orphans stored data.

Add a unit test that asserts the exact 11-key order and the SHA-256 of the serialized `SPECIALTY_TEMPLATES` payload against a golden file captured from the Node server.

findings.name: SPECIALTY_ALIASES — the complete 45-entry free-text → key map
findings.signature: const SPECIALTY_ALIASES = { ... }  // lines 399–456, exported but not used by any route
findings.behaviour:
45 entries, all keys already lowercase. Grouped by target: → ophthalmology: 'ophthalmology', 'ophthal', 'eye'. → cardiology: 'cardiology', 'cardiac', 'cardiovascular'. → neurology: 'neurology', 'neuro', 'neurological'. → orthopedics: 'orthopedics', 'orthopaedics', 'orthopedic surgery', 'ortho'. → pediatrics: 'pediatrics', 'paediatrics', 'peds', 'ped'. → pulmonology: 'pulmonology', 'pulmonary', 'respiratory', 'chest'. → internal_medicine: 'internal medicine', 'internal_medicine', 'im', 'general medicine', 'general practice', 'gp', 'family medicine'. → dermatology: 'dermatology', 'derm'. → obgyn: 'obgyn', 'ob/gyn', 'obstetrics', 'gynecology', 'gynaecology', 'obstetrics and gynecology', 'obstetrics & gynecology'. → psychiatry: 'psychiatry', 'psych', 'mental health'. → ent: 'ent', 'ent (ear, nose, throat)', 'otolaryngology', 'ear nose throat', 'ear, nose & throat'.

Coverage gap that matters: `PhysicianProfile.specialty` is `String` NOT NULL (server/prisma/schema.prisma:277) and is populated from server/prisma/seeds/specialties.json, which lists 35 specialties. Only 13 of those 35 resolve to a template: Internal Medicine, General Practice, Pediatrics, Obstetrics & Gynecology, Cardiology, Dermatology, ENT (Ear, Nose, Throat), Ophthalmology, Orthopedics, Neurology, Psychiatry, Pulmonology, Family Medicine. The other 22 (Urology, Nephrology, Gastroenterology, Endocrinology, Rheumatology, Oncology, Hematology, Anesthesiology, Radiology, Pathology, General Surgery, Plastic Surgery, Neurosurgery, Cardiac Surgery, Dentistry, Emergency Medicine, Sports Medicine, Geriatrics, Allergy & Immunology, Infectious Disease, Physical Medicine & Rehabilitation, Nuclear Medicine) get `template: null` — this is the DESIGNED behaviour, not a bug; the physician then picks manually from `allTemplates`. Note that both multi-word ENT and OB/GYN dropdown values were added specifically to match specialties.json verbatim (see the inline comments at lines 438 and 450). `SPECIALTY_ALIASES` is exported at line 516 but no route or client file imports it — only `getTemplateForSpecialty` reads it.
findings.portRecommendation: `private static readonly IReadOnlyDictionary<string, string> Aliases` inside the same static class, constructed with `StringComparer.Ordinal` (NOT OrdinalIgnoreCase — see the lowercasing quirk in the `getTemplateForSpecialty` finding; using an ignore-case comparer would change behaviour for inputs whose invariant-lowercase differs from a simple case fold). Keep it private unless you also mean to expose it; the Node export is dead.

findings.name: getTemplateForSpecialty(specialty) — exact matching semantics and the null/undefined split
findings.signature: function getTemplateForSpecialty(specialty)  // lines 462–466 — returns the FULL template object, or null, or (edge case) undefined
findings.behaviour:
Body is 2 lines: `if (!specialty) return null;` then `const key = SPECIALTY_ALIASES[specialty.toLowerCase().trim()]; return key ? SPECIALTY_TEMPLATES[key] : null;`

Matching is EXACT-after-normalization only — there is no substring, prefix, fuzzy, or token matching. Normalization order is `.toLowerCase()` THEN `.trim()` (harmless, but note the order if you mirror it literally). Verified behaviour:
- `null` / `undefined` / `''` → null (guard).
- `'   '` (whitespace only) → null (normalizes to `''`, which is not an alias key).
- `'Cardiology'` → cardiology template. `'  CARDIOLOGY  '` → cardiology template. `'Ophthalmology '` (trailing space) → ophthalmology template.
- `'ENT (Ear, Nose, Throat)'` → ent. `'Obstetrics & Gynecology'` → obgyn. `'im'` and `'IM'` → internal_medicine.
- `'cardio'` → null (NOT a prefix match — 'cardiac' and 'cardiovascular' are aliases, 'cardio' is not).
- `'Urology'`, `'Nephrology'`, `'General Surgery'`, `'Dentistry'` → null.
- `0` / `false` / `NaN` would hit the falsy guard → null; a non-string truthy value (e.g. a number `5`) would throw TypeError on `.toLowerCase()` — unreachable in practice because the column is a non-null String.
RETURN-TYPE QUIRK: it returns `null` on the guard and on a missed alias, but `undefined` for the two lowercase Object.prototype names `'constructor'` and `'__proto__'` (the alias lookup hits the prototype chain, is truthy, then `SPECIALTY_TEMPLATES[<function|Object.prototype>]` misses → undefined). `'toString'`, `'valueOf'`, `'hasOwnProperty'` return plain null because `.toLowerCase()` mangles them to 'tostring'/'valueof'/'hasownproperty' first. Both null and undefined are falsy, and both call sites coerce (`matched || null` at visits.js:47, `if (matched)` at visits.js:745), so the observable API behaviour is identical — no need to reproduce the null/undefined distinction.
When nothing matches, the caller emits `"template": null` (JSON null, not omitted, not `{}`).
findings.portRecommendation: `public static SpecialtyTemplate? GetTemplateForSpecialty(string? specialty)` on the static class. Body: `if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(specialty)) return null; var norm = specialty.ToLowerInvariant().Trim(); return Aliases.TryGetValue(norm, out var k) && All.TryGetValue(k, out var t) ? t : null;`. **Use `ToLowerInvariant()`, never `ToLower()`** — under tr-TR the alias `'im'` would become `'ım'` and every Internal-Medicine / GP / Family-Medicine physician would silently lose their template. Do NOT add fuzzy/contains matching as an 'improvement': it would start returning templates for the 22 currently-unmatched specialties (e.g. 'Cardiac Surgery' contains 'cardiac', 'Neurosurgery' contains 'neuro', 'Emergency Medicine' contains 'medicine') and change what the client renders.

findings.name: formatSpecialtyDataForPrompt(specialtyData, templateKey) — SOAP Objective context builder
findings.behaviour:
Produces a plain-text block injected into the SOAP user prompt (visits.js:787, under the heading `Structured Specialty Exam Data:`). Not part of any JSON response, but the .NET port must byte-match it or the LLM output drifts.

Algorithm: (1) return '' if `specialtyData` is falsy or `typeof !== 'object'` — so a JSON string or number yields ''; an ARRAY passes the typeof check (arrays are objects) but produces '' anyway since no numeric index matches a field key. (2) look up `SPECIALTY_TEMPLATES[templateKey]`; return '' if missing. (3) seed `lines = ['--- ' + template.label + ' ---']`. (4) For each section IN ORDER, collect per-field lines for each field IN ORDER where `specialtyData[field.key]` is not undefined, not null and not `''`. Line format is exactly `'  ' + field.label + ': ' + value + (field.unit ? ' ' + field.unit : '')` — TWO leading spaces, and the unit is preceded by a single space. (5) If a section produced ≥1 line, push `'[' + section.title + ']'` FIRST, then the field lines. Sections with no values emit nothing — not even the header. (6) `return lines.length > 1 ? lines.join('
') : ''` — if no section matched, the lone `--- label ---` header is DISCARDED and '' is returned. Lines are joined with `
` (LF), no trailing newline.

Truthiness quirks (verified): numeric `0` and boolean `false` ARE emitted (only undefined/null/'' are skipped) — e.g. `iop_os: 0` renders `  IOP (OS): 0 mmHg`, and `pupil_od: false` renders `  Pupil (OD): false`. Values are string-concatenated with JS semantics, so a nested object would render as `[object Object]` and an array as its comma-joined elements. Keys present in specialtyData that are not template fields (including the `__templateKey` sentinel and any stale field from a previously-selected template) are silently ignored — iteration is driven by the template, not by the data.

Verified sample — data `{__templateKey:'ophthalmology', iop_od:'14', iop_os:0, va_uncorrected_od:'6/6', va_corrected_os:'', fundus_od:null, pupil_od:false, unknown_key:'x'}` with key 'ophthalmology' returns exactly:
"--- Ophthalmology Exam ---
[Visual Acuity]
  VA Uncorrected (OD): 6/6
[Intraocular Pressure]
  IOP (OD): 14 mmHg
  IOP (OS): 0 mmHg
[Pupil & Refraction]
  Pupil (OD): false"
Empty-ish inputs all return '': `{}`, `{__templateKey:'ent'}`, `null`, an unknown templateKey, `[]`, `'x'`. The caller wraps the call in try/catch and falls back to '' (visits.js:751-755), and the prompt omits the whole `Structured Specialty Exam Data:` block when the result is '' (visits.js:787).
findings.portRecommendation:
`public static string FormatSpecialtyDataForPrompt(JsonObject? specialtyData, string? templateKey)` (or `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, JsonNode?>`). Build with a `List<string>` and `string.Join("
", …)` — explicit "
", never `Environment.NewLine`, or Windows hosting injects 
 and the prompt diverges. Emit `bool` as lowercase `"false"`/`"true"` (JS style, not .NET's "False") and numbers with `CultureInfo.InvariantCulture` so a comma decimal separator never appears. Reproduce the `lines.Count > 1` discard rule literally. Owner: same static class as the templates, called from the visits SOAP service.

findings.name: getFieldMapForPrompt(templateKey) — AI extraction field map
findings.behaviour:
Builds a JSON-LOOKING (but not JSON-parsed) block listing every valid field key for the second AI call that extracts structured exam data from dictation (visits.js:818, injected at visits.js:835 under `Fields:`).

Algorithm: return '' if `SPECIALTY_TEMPLATES[templateKey]` is missing (verified: `'nope'` → '', `undefined` → ''). Otherwise, for each section IN ORDER and each field IN ORDER, build `'  "' + field.key + '": "' + field.label + unit + type + '"'` where `unit = field.unit ? ' [' + field.unit + ']' : ''` and `type = field.type === 'select' ? ' (options: ' + field.options.join(', ') + ')' : ''`. Then return `'{
' + parts.join(',
') + '
}'`. Two leading spaces per line; comma-newline separators; no trailing comma; opening `{` and closing `}` on their own lines. Sections do NOT appear in the output — it is a flat map. Only `select` gets the options suffix; `date` and `number` get no marker beyond the unit bracket, so the AI is told `"lmp": "LMP"` with no hint that it is a date.

Verified output for 'obgyn':
{
  "lmp": "LMP",
  "gravida": "Gravida",
  "para": "Para",
  "gestational_age": "Gestational Age",
  "fundal_height": "Fundal Height [cm]",
  "fhr": "Fetal Heart Rate [bpm]",
  "presentation": "Presentation (options: Cephalic, Breech, Transverse, Oblique, Not assessed)",
  "cervical_exam": "Cervical Exam",
  "us_notes": "Ultrasound Notes",
  "gyn_exam": "Gynecologic Exam"
}
Unit examples: `"iop_od": "IOP (OD) [mmHg]"`, `"gcs": "GCS [/15]"`, `"fev1": "FEV1 [% predicted]"`.

FRAGILITY: `field.options.join(', ')` is unguarded — a `select` field without `options` would throw TypeError, caught by the surrounding try/catch at visits.js:873 which logs and skips extraction entirely. All 24 current select fields do have options, so this never fires today. Also, the output is only accidentally valid JSON: labels contain `(`, `)`, `/`, `&`, `>`, `+`, `°`, and em-dashes but no double quotes, so nothing escapes. `psychiatry.mood`'s PLACEHOLDER does contain `"depressed"` — placeholders are never emitted here, so it is safe; do not start emitting placeholders in the port.

Never returns '' for any of the 11 real keys (every template has ≥1 field), so the `if (fieldMap)` guard at visits.js:819 is always taken when `activeTemplateKey` is set.

findings.name: GET /api/visits/specialty-template — exact outgoing response shape (two distinct shapes)
findings.signature: router.get('/specialty-template', …)  // lines 32–55; mounted at /api/visits (index.js:216); behind router.use(authCheck) (line 21)
findings.behaviour:
Two DIFFERENT response shapes with different key sets — the port must reproduce both, including the missing key:

(A) No PhysicianProfile for `req.user.id` → HTTP 200, body exactly `{"template":null,"allTemplates":[]}`. The `specialty` key is ABSENT (not null). `allTemplates` is an EMPTY ARRAY, never null. This is the path patients hit.

(B) PhysicianProfile found → HTTP 200, body `{"template": <full template object|null>, "specialty": <physician.specialty string>, "allTemplates": [<11 summaries>]}` — key order exactly template, specialty, allTemplates. `template` is the COMPLETE template object (key/label/icon/sections, all nested sections and fields) as returned by `getTemplateForSpecialty(physician.specialty)`, coerced with `|| null`. `specialty` is the raw un-normalized free-text column value (non-null per schema; could be `""`). `allTemplates` is a RESHAPE of `Object.values(SPECIALTY_TEMPLATES).map(t => ({key, label, icon}))` — `sections` is DROPPED, key order key/label/icon, 11 entries always, in dictionary insertion order, regardless of the physician's specialty. Verified literal `allTemplates`:
[{"key":"ophthalmology","label":"Ophthalmology Exam","icon":"👁️"},{"key":"cardiology","label":"Cardiology Exam","icon":"🫀"},{"key":"neurology","label":"Neurological Exam","icon":"🧠"},{"key":"orthopedics","label":"Orthopedic Exam","icon":"🦴"},{"key":"pediatrics","label":"Pediatric Exam","icon":"👶"},{"key":"pulmonology","label":"Pulmonology Exam","icon":"🫁"},{"key":"internal_medicine","label":"Systems Review","icon":"🩺"},{"key":"dermatology","label":"Dermatology Exam","icon":"🧬"},{"key":"obgyn","label":"OB/GYN Exam","icon":"🤰"},{"key":"psychiatry","label":"Mental Status Exam","icon":"🧠"},{"key":"ent","label":"ENT Exam","icon":"🏥"}]
A full obgyn-physician response is 1854 UTF-8 bytes.

(C) Exception → HTTP 500 `{"error":"Failed to load specialty template"}`. No token → 401 `{"error":"No token provided"}`; bad token → 401 `{"error":"Invalid token"}` (server/src/middleware/auth.js:12,17).

No `cacheMiddleware` on this route and no Cache-Control header — the doc comment says "Cached on the frontend", and indeed both clients cache in React state, not HTTP. `app.set('etag','strong')` (index.js:39) means Express emits a strong ETag over the body, and `compression()` (index.js:36) gzips it. No date fields anywhere in this response.

Client consumption: client/src/components/SpecialtyExamCard.jsx:29-42 reads `res.data?.template` and `res.data?.allTemplates || []`; client/src/components/VisitTemplatePicker.jsx:85-95 reads `r.data?.allTemplates` and substitutes a HARD-CODED 11-entry FALLBACK_SPECIALTY_TEMPLATES (VisitTemplatePicker.jsx:19-31, currently identical to the server list) when the array is empty or the call fails. So if the .NET port ever returns an empty `allTemplates` for a physician, the picker silently shows the stale client copy instead.
findings.portRecommendation: Two DTOs, not one with conditional nulls — e.g. `record SpecialtyTemplateResponseNoProfile(SpecialtyTemplate? Template, IReadOnlyList<TemplateSummary> AllTemplates)` and `record SpecialtyTemplateResponse(SpecialtyTemplate? Template, string Specialty, IReadOnlyList<TemplateSummary> AllTemplates)`. Do NOT solve this with `[JsonIgnore(WhenWritingNull)]` on Specialty — the Node path B emits `"specialty": null`-equivalent behaviour only when the column is null, which the schema forbids, whereas path A omits the key even though it is a valid physician-less 200. `TemplateSummary(string Key, string Label, string Icon)`. Configure `JsonSerializerOptions.PropertyNamingPolicy = JsonNamingPolicy.CamelCase` and DefaultIgnoreCondition = Never for these. Owner: `VisitsController.GetSpecialtyTemplate()` in the Visits module, delegating to the static config class.

findings.name: GET /api/visits/specialty-template/:key — response shape and the prototype-key 200 leak
findings.behaviour:
Happy path: `SPECIALTY_TEMPLATES[req.params.key]` — the raw param, NOT lowercased, NOT trimmed, NOT alias-resolved. So only the 11 literal keys work; `'Ophthalmology'` (capital O) → 404. HTTP 200 body is `{"template": <full template object>}` — a single-key wrapper; the template is the same object the list endpoint puts in its `template` field. Miss → HTTP 404 `{"error":"Template not found"}`. Exception → HTTP 500 `{"error":"Failed to load template"}`. Behind the same authCheck.

QUIRK (verified) — JS prototype-chain leak: because the lookup is a bare bracket access on an object literal, `Object.prototype` member names return truthy and skip the 404. `GET /api/visits/specialty-template/__proto__` → HTTP 200 `{"template":{}}`. `GET .../constructor`, `.../toString`, `.../valueOf`, `.../isPrototypeOf`, `.../hasOwnProperty`, `.../propertyIsEnumerable`, `.../toLocaleString` → HTTP 200 with body `{}` (JSON.stringify drops function values, taking the whole `template` key with it). No information disclosure, but the status code is wrong and the response is malformed against the contract.

Client consumption (three call sites, all in client/src/components/SpecialtyExamCard.jsx): line 50 (switch to the `__templateKey` saved on the visit), line 86 (physician picks from the dropdown). All read `res.data?.template` and no-op / `setTemplate(null)` otherwise — so both the `{}` and `{"template":{}}` bodies are effectively inert, and a 404 (axios reject → `.catch`) is handled too. Nothing in the client ever requests a non-literal key.
findings.portRecommendation: `public IActionResult GetSpecialtyTemplate(string key)` returning `Ok(new { template })` / `NotFound(new { error = "Template not found" })`. A `Dictionary.TryGetValue` naturally returns false for `__proto__`/`toString`, so the .NET port will emit 404 where Node emits 200 — treat that as an intentional, documented divergence rather than replicating the leak: it is unreachable from the client and the client's `.catch` path already handles 404. Flag it in the port's contract-diff notes so a future JSON-diff harness doesn't chase it. Route the literal segment explicitly (`[HttpGet("specialty-template/{key}")]`) — see the route-precedence finding.

findings.name: BLOCKER for byte-identical JSON: System.Text.Json's default encoder escapes 12 emoji, 19 '&', 8 '+', 5 em-dashes, 1 '°' and 1 '>'
findings.behaviour:
Express `res.json` uses `JSON.stringify`, which escapes only `"`, `\`, control chars and lone surrogates — it emits every other character as raw UTF-8 (`Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8`). `System.Text.Json`'s DEFAULT `JavaScriptEncoder` escapes all non-ASCII plus the HTML-sensitive set `< > & ' " +`. A full scan of `JSON.stringify(SPECIALTY_TEMPLATES)` found these characters that would diverge:
- `&` × 19 — section titles "Pupil & Refraction", "Cranial Nerves & Motor", "Sensory, Reflexes & Coordination", "Development & Nutrition", "General & HEENT", "Chest & Cardiovascular", "Abdomen & Extremities", "Appearance & Behavior", "Mood & Thought", "Perception & Cognition", "Hearing & Nose", "Throat & Neck"; options "Oriented to person & place", "Open & flat", "Open & bulging", "Open & sunken", "Active & alert", "Logical & goal-directed"; placeholder "A&O x3, CN II-XII intact, normal gait".
- `+` × 8 — options "1+", "2+", "3+", "4+" (cardiology.peripheral_edema); placeholders "2+ symmetric" (neurology.reflexes and internal_medicine.extremities), "Soft, non-tender, no organomegaly, BS+", "32+4 weeks".
- `—` U+2014 × 5 — all pulmonology.dyspnea_mmrc options ("0 — No breathlessness" … "4 — Too breathless to leave house").
- `°` U+00B0 × 1 — orthopedics.rom_active placeholder "Flexion 0-120°, full extension".
- `>` U+003E × 1 — ent.hearing placeholder "Weber midline, Rinne AC>BC bilateral".
- 12 emoji code points across the 11 icons, including the U+FE0F variation selector on ophthalmology's 👁️ (which is a SEPARATE code point — a naive re-typing of the emoji drops it and changes both the JSON bytes and the rendered glyph width).
Also present and safely identical in both serializers: `"` inside psychiatry.mood's placeholder `Patient-reported (e.g. "depressed", "anxious")` (both emit `\"`), and `/` in "OB/GYN Exam", "Spirometry / PFT", "6/6", "5/5", "/15", "L/min", "RAPD -, 3mm" (JSON.stringify does not escape `/`, and neither does STJ).
findings.portRecommendation: Set `options.Encoder = JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping` on the JsonSerializerOptions used for these endpoints (ideally app-wide in `AddJsonOptions`, since the same hazard applies to every Arabic `nameAr` string elsewhere in this API). `UnicodeRanges.All` alone is NOT enough — it fixes the emoji and em-dash and degree sign but still escapes `&`, `+` and `>` to `&`, `+`, `>`. Store the icons in an embedded JSON file copied byte-for-byte from the Node source (or as `👁️`-style escapes in C# string literals) rather than pasting emoji into .cs, to survive an editor that normalizes or strips variation selectors. Add a golden-file byte comparison test against a live Node response — this is the single most likely place the port silently breaks the contract.

findings.name: BLOCKER for byte-identical JSON: optional field/section keys must be OMITTED, never emitted as null
findings.behaviour:
`JSON.stringify` drops absent/undefined properties entirely. Across all 117 fields there are exactly 4 distinct property-set signatures, verified by inspection:
- `["key","label","type","placeholder"]` — 82 fields
- `["key","label","type","unit","placeholder"]` — 11 fields (unit precedes placeholder)
- `["key","label","type","options"]` — 23 fields (all 24 select fields except… all 23 select-with-no-placeholder; every select field lacks a placeholder)
- `["key","label","type"]` — 1 field: `obgyn.lmp` (type `date`, no unit, no options, no placeholder)
And 2 section signatures: `["title","paired","fields"]` × 6 and `["title","fields"]` × 28. `paired` is only ever the literal `true`; `false` never appears.
So NO field ever carries both `unit` and `options`, no select field carries a `placeholder`, and only one field carries none of the three. The client tests these with truthiness (`field.unit && …`, `(field.options || [])`, `section.paired ? '1fr 1fr' : …` in SpecialtyExamCard.jsx:210,265,297) so it tolerates explicit nulls functionally — but the JSON bytes would differ, which is the stated contract.
findings.portRecommendation: On the JsonSerializerOptions: `DefaultIgnoreCondition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull`, with `Unit`, `Options` and `Placeholder` declared as nullable (`string?`, `IReadOnlyList<string>?`) and `Paired` as `bool?` (never `bool` with a false default — that would emit `"paired":false` on 28 sections). Beware that a repo-wide `WhenWritingNull` would also break the `{"template":null,…}` responses, which MUST emit an explicit null: either scope the options to this controller, or keep the global policy `Never` and put `[JsonIgnore(Condition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull)]` on the four optional members individually. The latter is safer and is what I'd recommend.

findings.name: visit.specialtyData persistence, the __templateKey sentinel, and all-values-are-strings
findings.signature: specialtyData Json?  // schema.prisma:649 on model Visit; written at visits.js:462 (PUT /:id) and visits.js:886 (generate-soap)
findings.behaviour:
Nullable JSON column, no shape validation anywhere. `PUT /api/visits/:id` does `if (specialtyData !== undefined) updateData.specialtyData = specialtyData;` (visits.js:462) and then `return res.json(updated)` — the raw Prisma Visit row, so `specialtyData` comes back to the client as a nested JSON OBJECT, not a JSON string. Same in `GET /api/visits/:id` (visits.js:369: `res.json({ ...visit, patientUser, isPhysician })`). Sending explicit `null` in the body WRITES null (only `undefined`/absent is skipped). A COMPLETED visit rejects any specialtyData write: the follow-up-only guard at visits.js:411-420 does not list `specialtyData` in its `=== undefined` checks, so a body containing specialtyData plus followUpDate still passes `isFollowUpOnly` and then SILENTLY DISCARDS the specialtyData (only `followUpData` is applied) — a real quirk worth preserving or at least noting.

Content contract in practice: `Record<string, string>`. Every FieldRenderer input binds `e.target.value` (SpecialtyExamCard.jsx:293,301,315,325) so even `number` and `date` fields store STRINGS — `lmp` is a `"YYYY-MM-DD"` string, never a Date or ISO timestamp, and there is no Date anywhere in specialtyData. The AI extraction path coerces explicitly with `String(value)` (visits.js:863). The client sends specialtyData only when at least one value is non-empty (`hasSpecData` at client/src/pages/VisitDetailPage.jsx:154,182-186,205-208), so an all-blank form leaves the column untouched rather than writing `{}`.

`__templateKey` is a RESERVED sentinel key stored INSIDE specialtyData (not a column): written client-side on template switch (SpecialtyExamCard.jsx:90) and stripped on template clear (SpecialtyExamCard.jsx:80), written server-side after successful AI extraction (visits.js:868). It is filtered out of key-count logic (visits.js:734, VisitDetailPage.jsx:231) and is never a template field key, so `formatSpecialtyDataForPrompt` never prints it. Switching templates does NOT purge the previous template's field values — stale keys accumulate in the column and are simply ignored by the template-driven renderer and formatter.
findings.portRecommendation: Map to `nvarchar(max)` with EF Core `.HasColumnType("nvarchar(max)")` and a `JsonDocument`/`JsonObject` property (or `.HasConversion` to `JsonNode`), and make sure the API layer writes it into the response as a raw JSON object — a `string` property would serialize as an escaped JSON STRING (`"specialtyData":"{\"iop_od\":\"14\"}"`) and break the client. Never round-trip it through a typed `Dictionary<string,string>`: that would drop `__templateKey` ordering/unknown keys and reject any non-string value already in production data. Preserve the completed-visit silent-discard behaviour, or fix it deliberately and note the divergence. Owner: the Visits EF configuration plus `VisitsController.Update`.

findings.name: POST /api/visits/:id/generate-soap — 4-tier template resolution and the specialty fields on the response
findings.signature: router.post('/:id/generate-soap', aiUsageCheck('soap'), …)  // lines 674–938; template resolution lines 727–747
findings.behaviour:
This is the only consumer of `formatSpecialtyDataForPrompt` and `getFieldMapForPrompt`. `activeTemplateKey` is resolved in strict priority order, first hit wins:
1. `req.body.specialtyKey` — accepted only if it is a real key in SPECIALTY_TEMPLATES (visits.js:728). The client sends `activeSpecialtyTemplate || specialtyData?.__templateKey || null` (VisitDetailPage.jsx:217).
2. `visit.specialtyData.__templateKey` — again only if it names a real template (visits.js:730).
3. HEURISTIC key sniffing (visits.js:732-742): take `Object.keys(visit.specialtyData)` minus `__templateKey`; if non-empty, iterate SPECIALTY_TEMPLATES in dictionary order and pick the FIRST template where ≥2 of the data keys are among that template's field keys (`matchCount >= 2`, `break`). One matching key is NOT enough. Because all 117 field keys are globally unique (verified: zero collisions), this is deterministic and unambiguous — but the iteration order means ophthalmology is tested first, so preserving dictionary order matters here too.
4. `getTemplateForSpecialty(physician.specialty)?.key` (visits.js:743-746).
If all four miss, `activeTemplateKey` stays null: no `Structured Specialty Exam Data:` block is added to the SOAP prompt and the entire second (extraction) AI call is skipped.

Extraction merge (visits.js:844-872): the model's reply is scanned with `/\{[\s\S]*\}/` (greedy — strips code fences), JSON.parsed inside a try/catch that only warns on failure. Then `existing = {...visit.specialtyData}`, and for each extracted entry that is not ''/null/undefined, `existing[key] = String(value)` — NOTE: extracted keys are NOT validated against the template's field keys, so a hallucinated key is persisted verbatim into the column. Only if ≥1 field was added does it set `existing.__templateKey = activeTemplateKey` and assign `mergedSpecialtyData`; otherwise `mergedSpecialtyData` stays null and the column is left alone.

Success response (visits.js:894-909), key order exactly: `message`, `subjective`, `objective`, `assessment`, `plan`, `aiProvider`, `aiModel`, `enhanced` (`!!enhance`, always a real boolean), `aiUsage` (`req.aiUsage || null`), `specialtyData` (`mergedSpecialtyData || null` — the FULL merged object including `__templateKey`, or JSON null when nothing was extracted), `specialtyKey` (`activeTemplateKey || null`). The `message` string differs by `enhance`: 'SOAP note generated with GPT-4o (enhanced). Review and edit as needed.' vs 'SOAP note generated by AI. Review and edit as needed.'.
AI-failure fallback response (visits.js:925-932) has a DIFFERENT and SHORTER key set: `message` ('SOAP note generated (template — AI unavailable). Edit as needed.' — contains an em-dash, see the escaping finding), `subjective`, `objective`, `assessment`, `plan`, `aiProvider` ('template'). `aiModel`, `enhanced`, `aiUsage`, `specialtyData` and `specialtyKey` are ALL ABSENT — not null. The client reads `res.data.specialtyData` and `res.data.specialtyKey` defensively (VisitDetailPage.jsx:229-234), so absence is safe, but the bytes differ.
Other statuses: 404 `{"error":"Visit not found"}`, 403 `{"error":"Not your visit"}`, 400 `{"error":"No notes or transcript to process"}` (when both rawNotes and rawTranscript are falsy), 500 `{"error":"Failed to generate SOAP note"}`.
findings.portRecommendation: Put the 4-tier resolution in a dedicated `SpecialtyTemplateResolver` service (Visits module) with the priority encoded as an explicit ordered chain, and unit-test tier 3's `>= 2` threshold and first-match-in-dictionary-order semantics. Two separate response records for the AI-success and template-fallback paths (do not merge them behind nullable properties — the fallback omits five keys). Keep the `String(value)` coercion and the deliberate absence of key validation on extracted data so existing rows stay reproducible.

findings.name: Route precedence: ASP.NET Core will resolve /api/visits/... differently than Express and can change behaviour
findings.signature: router.use(authCheck) at line 21; /specialty-template at 32; /specialty-template/:key at 61; /:id at 272; /follow-ups-due at 1244 (AFTER /:id)
findings.behaviour: Express matches in registration order. The two specialty-template routes are registered FIRST (lines 32, 61), so they win over `GET /:id` (line 272) — correct today, but only by ordering luck. The same file shows what happens when the luck runs out: `GET /follow-ups-due` is registered at line 1244, AFTER `GET /:id`, so in Node it is DEAD — every request to `/api/visits/follow-ups-due` is served by `GET /:id` with `id === 'follow-ups-due'`, which finds no Visit and returns 404 `{"error":"Visit not found"}` (and its `cacheMiddleware(30)` never runs). ASP.NET Core routing scores literal segments above `{id}` parameter segments regardless of declaration order, so a straight port will suddenly START serving `/follow-ups-due` with real data and a 30s cache — an unannounced behaviour change on an endpoint the client may or may not still call.
findings.portRecommendation: Declare the literal routes explicitly (`[HttpGet("specialty-template")]`, `[HttpGet("specialty-template/{key}")]`) — .NET precedence gets these right for free. But audit `/follow-ups-due` before shipping: decide whether the port should keep returning 404 (add an explicit route constraint or leave the endpoint unimplemented) or intentionally light it up, and check whether the client calls it. Do not let route-precedence differences be discovered by the client. Owner: `VisitsController` route attributes plus a port-diff note.

findings.name: Port recommendation: embedded JSON resource over hand-written records (with the records as the deserialization target)
findings.behaviour: The payload is 117 fields / 34 sections / 24 option arrays / 11 emoji icons of pure literal data, and the contract is byte-identical JSON. Hand-transcribing it into C# object initializers puts ~500 string literals through a human and an editor — the exact failure modes are the U+FE0F variation selector on 👁️ silently dropped, an em-dash normalized to a hyphen, `Systems Review` 'corrected' to `Internal Medicine Exam`, a `placeholder` accidentally added to a select field, `paired: false` materialized on 28 sections, or one of the 11 unit strings retyped as `%predicted`. None of those fail to compile and none fail a smoke test — they show up as a client that renders a slightly wrong form.
findings.portRecommendation:
RECOMMENDED: a hybrid — records as the type model, embedded JSON as the data.
1. Copy the data verbatim out of the Node process (`node -e "console.log(JSON.stringify(require('./src/config/specialtyTemplates').SPECIALTY_TEMPLATES, null, 2))"`) into `Tebrazi.Api/Configuration/specialtyTemplates.json`, checked in as an `<EmbeddedResource>` with `<Utf8Encoding>` preserved. Do the same for the 45-entry alias map (`specialtyAliases.json`). Never retype the emoji or em-dashes.
2. `static class SpecialtyTemplates` with a static constructor that reads the resource once and deserializes into `List<SpecialtyTemplate>` (preserving order) plus a `Dictionary<string, SpecialtyTemplate>(StringComparer.Ordinal)` index; expose `IReadOnlyList<SpecialtyTemplate> Ordered`, `IReadOnlyDictionary<string, SpecialtyTemplate> All`, and the three functions `GetTemplateForSpecialty`, `FormatSpecialtyDataForPrompt`, `GetFieldMapForPrompt`.
3. Serialize back out through the SAME record types with `Encoder = JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping`, camelCase naming, and per-member `WhenWritingNull` — so the response bytes are generated, not passed through, and the records enforce property order.
4. CI test: assert `SHA256(serialize(Ordered.Select(summary)))` and `SHA256(serialize(All[key]))` for all 11 keys against golden files captured from the running Node server, plus golden-string tests for `GetFieldMapForPrompt(k)` for all 11 keys and a table of `FormatSpecialtyDataForPrompt` cases (including the 0/false/''/null/stale-key/only-__templateKey cases documented above).
Why not pure embedded JSON served as a pass-through blob: it would be byte-perfect by construction, but you lose compile-time safety for the resolver and formatters (which must walk sections/fields in order and read `unit`/`options`/`label`), and `allTemplates` needs a real reshape rather than a substring of the file. Why not pure records: transcription risk, above. Owner: `Tebrazi.Api/Configuration/` (or `Tebrazi.Domain/Visits/Config/`), referenced by the Visits controller and the SOAP generation service — keep it out of the AI service so the two prompt formatters stay next to the data they format.
